baseline.prior_evidence_policy: Historical partial results are context only. They do not qualify the final release artifacts.

milestones.title: Audit and acceptance inventory
milestones.exit: Every requirement, supported platform, provider build, test entry point, and environmental dependency has an owner and an evidence path.

milestones.title: Shared executable Core contracts
milestones.exit: One immutable Core wheel passes R4 conformance and R3 history tests in both installed consumers; executable contract status is evidence based.

milestones.title: Composition persistence and authority
milestones.exit: HTTP-only MCP, additive migrations, canonical identity, scoped tickets, session capabilities, and operator authorization pass their positive and negative cases.

milestones.title: Inventory consent and reusable bindings
milestones.exit: Local and remote onboarding creates an approved binding through public entry points and reuses it without repeating technical setup.

milestones.title: Canonical operation dispatcher
milestones.exit: All user intents use one durable admission and dispatch path; loss of a response, cancellation, or retry never creates a second native effect.

milestones.title: Embedded execution through the product
milestones.exit: An installed Nexus and Core open, submit, control, observe, and close a local runtime using canonical admission with no Connector application installed.

milestones.title: Remote daemon lanes leases and execution
milestones.exit: The real Connector daemon performs R4 negotiation, paginated reconciliation, correlated attach and lease installation, and remote open and controls from the Nexus dispatcher.

milestones.title: Durable events receipts and replay
milestones.exit: Events and receipts survive restart and reconnect with contiguous post-commit ACKs, bounded journals, explicit gaps, and publisher recovery without a new native event.

milestones.title: Canonical decisions and native input
milestones.exit: An authorized decision produces exactly one native application and a recoverable receipt while preserving full request identity, namespace, and sensitive input rules.

milestones.title: Direct tools and governed work
milestones.exit: Direct MCP HTTP and the qualified Pi native bridge reach the same authorized domain with exclusive consumption, causal results, and no Connector MCP proxy.

milestones.title: Complete UI CLI and US English
milestones.exit: Human and headless user journeys pass through the actual UI and CLI; all application-authored visible and returned text is US English.

milestones.title: Recovery revocation shutdown and limits
milestones.exit: Process crashes, partitions, rotation, disk pressure, and shutdown preserve ownership and uncertainty without unbounded queues or unauthorized effects.

milestones.title: Migration cutover and removal of duplicate execution
milestones.exit: Legacy data and active ownership migrate with restartable checkpoints and verified rollback; obsolete execution paths are removed after demonstrated parity.

milestones.title: Final artifacts and complete acceptance
milestones.exit: The immutable three-repository release tuple passes all applicable TR4, TN, J, language, platform, provider, and installed-product campaigns with no unresolved required test.

additional_requirements.requirement: All application-authored UI, accessibility, CLI, API, MCP, WebSocket, error, diagnostic, and return messages use US English, including legacy surfaces.

acceptance_policy.test_assignment: Each original scenario is assigned to the latest closing milestone of its source task IDs and is reassessed on final artifacts in M13.
acceptance_policy.not_applicable_requires: A normative capability or platform exclusion, its negative test, and an explicit recorded rationale; missing infrastructure is NOT_RUN, never NOT_APPLICABLE.
acceptance_policy.commit_policy: Commit coherent tested increments and push feature/v0.2.0 in each changed repository; milestone closure requires all acceptance evidence, independently of commit count.

execution_batches.title: Baseline and acceptance evidence
execution_batches.acceptance: Each requirement has an owner, public caller, collectible test or explicit test work, environment and evidence; preserve failed attempts and known defects. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Shared contract
execution_batches.acceptance: Installed conformance covers all seven actions, errors, targeting and lease authority, preserves historical R3, and uses the same hashed Core wheel in both consumers. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Reusable onboarding
execution_batches.acceptance: Public first and repeated onboarding preserve identity, explicit runtime grants, consent, replay, denial and concurrent revision checks. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Opening and outbox
execution_batches.acceptance: Canonical admission and outbox are atomic; lease installation precedes native preparation; lost responses preserve operation IDs and control remains available under saturation. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Embedded cycle
execution_batches.acceptance: An installed Nexus without the Connector application executes the embedded lifecycle through public callers, with technical-peer and real-provider evidence classified separately. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Remote cycle
execution_batches.acceptance: Automatic persisted daemon composition, protected configuration, ticket rotation, lease renewal and nonempty paginated reconciliation pass in independent product processes. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

steps.title: Approved configuration and protected launch environment
Automatic lane attachment and execution ownership
Nonempty paginated recovery and publication obligations
Installed integration through independent product processes

execution_batches.title: Durable observation
execution_batches.acceptance: Durable receipts and events recover after restart without a new native event; duplicates, gaps, lost acknowledgments and namespace collisions are covered. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Decisions and input
execution_batches.acceptance: Canonical approval and input through public callers cause one authorized native application under concurrency, timeout, denial and restart. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Tools and domain
execution_batches.acceptance: Native context/claim/complete and managed MCP share canonical claims and causal results; replay, cross-channel contention, revocation and independent tools-only operation are proven. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: User journeys and US English
execution_batches.acceptance: Complete browser and human/headless CLI journeys pass; TLANG-01 through TLANG-04 cover all application-authored US English text and packaged resources. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Failures and limits
execution_batches.acceptance: Fault barriers, process death, partitions and storage pressure prove authority, ownership, containment and bounded memory, queues and shutdown; all CN5 findings are covered. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Installation upgrades
execution_batches.acceptance: Representative legacy data and pending sessions survive interrupted and repeated migration, owner drain, cutover, joint database/journal restore and verified rollback. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.

execution_batches.title: Complete delivery
execution_batches.acceptance: The frozen three-repository release tuple passes all mandatory scenarios, declared platforms and real-provider local/remote matrices, with G0-G3 closed and runbooks delivered. Original task and milestone dependencies remain mandatory.
